regions.source:
# frozen_string_literal: true

class ReviewOwnerRows
  def self.call
    ReviewDocument.where.not(owner_id: nil).order(:id).limit(20).map do |document|
      [document.title, document.owner.name]
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

class ReviewDocument < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :owner, class_name: 'ReviewOwner', optional: true
  default_scope { where(archived: false) }
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

class ReviewOwner < ApplicationRecord
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe ReviewOwnerRows do
  it 'returns each document with its owner name' do
    owner = ReviewOwner.create!(name: 'Alex')
    ReviewDocument.create!(title: 'Agenda', owner: owner)
    expect(described_class.call).to eq([['Agenda', 'Alex']])
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

class CreateReviewBankTables < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.0]
  def change
    create_table :review_invitations do |t|
      t.string :token, null: false
    end
    add_index :review_invitations, :token, unique: true
    create_table :review_owners do |t|
      t.string :name, null: false
    end
    create_table :review_documents do |t|
      t.string :title, null: false
      t.boolean :archived, null: false, default: false
      t.integer :reviewer_id, null: false, default: 1
      t.references :owner, foreign_key: { to_table: :review_owners, on_delete: :nullify }
    end
    add_index :review_documents, :reviewer_id
    create_table :review_products do |t|
      t.integer :price_cents, null: false
      t.timestamps
    end
    create_table :review_wallets do |t|
      t.integer :balance, null: false, default: 0
      t.integer :limit, null: false, default: 1000
    end
  end
end

job_failure_impact.instructions: If a job in this change fails or runs twice, what happens?
criteria: no jobs, or retries cleanly with no side effect
duplicate work with no external effect
duplicate external side effect (email, notification, API call)
duplicate charge, double write, or corrupted data

job_not_idempotent.instructions: Does a job produce a different or harmful result if it runs twice with the same arguments?

job_complex_args.instructions: Does a Sidekiq-native job take an ActiveRecord object, a Proc, or a nested structure as an argument instead of simple IDs and primitives? Active Job arguments may pass records via GlobalID.

job_enqueued_inside_transaction.instructions: Does the change enqueue a job inside a transaction on a Rails version or adapter that does not defer the enqueue until commit, so the job may run before the write is visible?

job_assumes_record_exists.instructions: Does a job assume the record it was enqueued for still exists and is in the same state?

job_no_retry_strategy.instructions: Does a job with side effects (email, payment, external API) lack an explicit retry or dead-letter decision?

job_read_modify_write.instructions: Does the change read a value, compute from it, and write it back without a lock or atomic update?

job_unbounded_fanout.instructions: Does the change enqueue one job per record for a collection with no upper bound?

job_shared_mutable_state.instructions: Does the change mutate class-level or global state that multiple threads or job workers could touch?

job_long_running_no_checkpoint.instructions: Does a job process a large batch with no progress checkpoint, so a restart repeats all the work?

obs_debuggability.instructions: If this change fails in production, how much would an engineer have to work with?
criteria: error reported with context, ids, and the original cause
error reported, context thin
logged only, no report
silent, swallowed, or a vague message

obs_cause_lost.instructions: Does a rescue raise a new exception in a way that drops the original as `cause`?

obs_error_not_reported.instructions: Does the change handle an error without reporting it through `Rails.error` or the app's error reporter?

obs_log_without_context.instructions: Does the change log a message with no identifying context (record id, user, request, job)?

obs_new_integration_uninstrumented.instructions: Does the change add an external call, job, or critical path with no instrumentation, event, or metric?

obs_error_message_vague.instructions: Does a raised error's message omit which record, operation, or input failed?

obs_filter_parameters_missing.instructions: Does the change add a param or attribute that is sensitive without adding it to `filter_parameters`?

obs_exception_outside_hierarchy.instructions: Does the change define an exception class that does not inherit from the app's base error?

obs_retries_exhausted_unhandled.instructions: Does a job with side effects lack a `sidekiq_retries_exhausted` or `discard_on` decision?

obs_wrong_log_level.instructions: Does the change log an expected condition at error level, or a failure at info or debug?

repo_different_approach.instructions: Does the change solve its problem in a different way than the sibling files solve the same kind of problem?

repo_naming_drift.instructions: Does the change name methods, variables, or classes differently than the naming pattern in the sibling files?

repo_wrong_layer.instructions: Does the change put logic in a different layer than the codebase puts that kind of logic?

repo_reinvents_local_helper.instructions: Does the change introduce a helper, concern, or pattern when an equivalent already exists in the codebase?

repo_ignores_base_class.instructions: Does the change bypass a base class, concern, or callback that the sibling files rely on?

repo_inconsistent_error_handling.instructions: Does the change handle errors differently than the sibling files do?

repo_inconsistent_return_shape.instructions: Does the change return a different shape (result object, boolean, record, raise) than the sibling files return for the same kind of operation?

repo_fit.instructions: How well does this match the surrounding code?
criteria: indistinguishable
same approach, small style differences
recognizably different approach
contradicts an established pattern

rollout_user_visibility.instructions: How much will a user notice this change?
criteria: invisible
cosmetic or wording
changes a flow, form, or response shape
removes or replaces something users rely on

rollout_behavior_change_scope.instructions: How much existing behavior does this change alter?
criteria: none, purely additive
edge cases of existing behavior
the main path of recently added behavior
the main path of long-standing behavior that users or other systems likely depend on

rollout_code_needs_migration_first.instructions: Does the code depend on a schema change in the same diff, so it breaks if deployed before the migration runs?

rollout_migration_breaks_old_code.instructions: Does a migration remove or rename something the currently deployed code still reads or writes?

rollout_not_reversible.instructions: Would reverting this deploy leave data in a state the previous code cannot handle?

rollout_no_flag_for_risky_change.instructions: Does the change alter user-facing behavior for everyone at once with no feature flag or gradual path?

rollout_backfill_in_request.instructions: Does the change rely on a backfill or data fix that has not been run?

rollout_config_change_untracked.instructions: Does the change require an environment variable, credential, or infrastructure change not present in the diff?

rollout_public_api_no_deprecation.instructions: Does the change remove or rename a public method, option, or route without a deprecation path?

rollout_scheduled_task_untracked.instructions: Does the change add a cron or scheduled task with no deploy step recorded?

rollout_destructive_migration_no_backup.instructions: Does a migration destroy or rewrite data with no backup step recorded for the deploy?

blast_data_reach.instructions: How far does this change's effect on stored data reach?
criteria: only records the change itself creates
existing records of one user or account
records shared across many users or processes
global, cross-tenant, or every row of a table

blast_shared_data_write.instructions: Does the change write to data that other code paths in the state also read or write?

blast_dangling_reference.instructions: Does the change rename or remove a method, column, constant, or route that something else still references?

blast_callback_reach.instructions: Does the change alter a callback, validation, scope, or default that fires on writes from other code paths?

blast_race_condition.instructions: Could two concurrent requests or jobs running this change produce a different result than running them one after the other?

blast_shared_record.instructions: Does the change mutate a record many users or processes share (account, settings, counter, cache row)?

blast_orphans_records.instructions: Does the change delete or nullify records that other records reference?

blast_changes_serialized_shape.instructions: Does the change alter the shape of data that is serialized, cached, or stored as JSON, so existing stored values no longer match?

hygiene_unrelated_changes.instructions: Does the diff include changes unrelated to the stated intent?

hygiene_undescribed_behavior_change.instructions: Does the diff change behavior that the description does not mention?

hygiene_dead_code.instructions: Does the change leave behind code, comments, or feature flags that nothing references?

hygiene_debug_artifacts.instructions: Does the change include `binding.pry`, `puts`, `console.log`, `.only`, `focus: true`, or commented-out code?

hygiene_todo_without_owner.instructions: Does the change add a TODO, FIXME, or HACK with no linked issue or owner?

hygiene_silent_default_change.instructions: Does the change alter a default value, timeout, limit, or configuration constant without calling it out?

hygiene_comment_explains_what.instructions: Does the change add a comment that restates what the code does rather than why?

hygiene_commit_message_why.instructions: Does the commit message say what changed without saying why, or omit the issue it fixes?

hygiene_cosmetic_only.instructions: Is the change purely cosmetic, adding nothing to stability, functionality, or testability?

hygiene_changelog_missing.instructions: Does a behavior change or new feature lack a changelog or release-note entry?

hygiene_docs_stale.instructions: Does the change alter a documented public method, option, or config without updating its documentation?

hygiene_moves_logic_out_of_coverage.instructions: Does the change move logic into a new code path that existing tests no longer exercise?

dep_upgrade_no_reason.instructions: Does a dependency upgrade lack a reason or a link to the dependency's changelog?

hygiene_can_simplify.instructions: Could this code be made simpler while still meeting the standards shown in the sibling files?

hygiene_can_optimize.instructions: Could this code be made faster or cheaper while still meeting the standards shown in the sibling files?

disposition.instructions: What is the most useful next step for this change?

criteria.simplify: correct but could be simpler within codebase standards
criteria.optimize: correct but leaves a clear performance improvement on the table
criteria.rework: has a correctness, security, or data problem that polish will not fix

primary_concern.instructions: If one reviewer should look at this first, which domain is it?

criteria.observability: cannot be debugged when it fails

change_kind.instructions: What kind of change is this?

criteria.mixed: more than one of the above in one diff
